title: ARC Prize public website audit — handoff for Matt and coding assistant
scope: Public production pages, navigation, published source/data, result archives and resource destinations. Manual browser checks focused on ARC1/2 task inspection and the ARC3 task index, with an ARC Explainer reference comparison.

priorities.P1: Fix first: core visitor workflow currently fails or defaults to unusable data.
priorities.P2: Next: data coverage/provenance, broken research journeys, and accessibility.
priorities.P3: Editorial or product improvement; not a blocker or commitment.

not_covered: Private source repository or server implementation
Paid inference, accounts, submissions, donations or forms end-to-end
Full pedagogical/playability review of every external game

tickets.title: Default ARC3 task explorer exceeds model-query body limit
tickets.observation: The live browser shows Failed to load ARC-AGI-3 session data. Public /api/models lookup with all 61 published configs, compact JSON exactly 1984 bytes, returns HTTP 500: error decoding json: http: request body too large. One-config 82-byte control returns HTTP 200 and 25 session rows. Changing Content-Type alone does not fix full request.
reproduction: Open /tasks anonymously with its default ARC3 tab.
Observe the session-data error and the misleading 1–25 of 25 footer.
Reproduce the recorded full-config request and one-config control in evidence.json (model_query_reproduction).
tickets.proposed_fix: Agree on an all-config query contract, bounded batching/selection, or a sufficient validated body limit; retain useful error handling. Do not assume adding Content-Type is sufficient.
acceptance_checks: Fresh anonymous /tasks shows ARC3 scores/replay links without the error.
A lookup covering every current config succeeds, with an automated growth case.
Oversized/invalid requests get explicit appropriate errors; no silent empty matrix.
tickets.qualification: The observed request is rejected for size. The exact server limit and private handler implementation were not inspected. Public source locator: tasks-index.formatted.js:328-354; original minified bundle is the public source
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Default featured models have no rows in the ARC1/2 task feed
tickets.observation: The task feed has 20061 rows, 42 model IDs and 514 distinct tasks. Every one of the five current featured catalogue IDs has zero matching rows. Bundle defaults to catalogue featured IDs and renders missing joins as N/A. Live browser confirms first 25 rows all N/A.
reproduction: Open /tasks?v=2 in a fresh session.
Observe N/A for every featured model in the first 25 rows.
Choose GPT 5.2 alone in the model selector; historical results and costs populate. Check ARC1 coverage using the same feed.
tickets.proposed_fix: Choose defaults from models with records for the active dataset, disclose coverage, and update the result feed. Keep explicitly selected absent models distinguishable from failures.
acceptance_checks: Fresh ARC1 and ARC2 tabs have usable default results or a clear source-coverage message.
Switching dataset recalculates applicable featured coverage.
Catalogue changes cannot turn the default matrix into entirely N/A columns unnoticed.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Task-level results lack current coverage and provenance
tickets.observation: 0934a4d8 JSON contains 74 rows/41 distinct model IDs:35 ARC1 rows,39 ARC2 rows. There are no ARC2 Pass rows, yet official HF Opus4.6 high file for this exact task has both attempts correct. Task JSON only contains provider/modelId/dataset/passed/totalCost; no source revision, import date, attempt IDs or answer grids. Live browser inspection found no result links or model/dataset/outcome filters. Astra’s current model page reports this task across six reasoning settings, but none appears in the task summary.
reproduction: Open /tasks/0934a4d8 and inspect Model Performance.
Compare its ARC2 rows with the linked official Opus 4.6 HF file.
Follow task 0934a4d8 from the Astra results page; the destination does not retain its model/reasoning selection and the table omits Astra.
tickets.proposed_fix: Generate model-page and task-page summaries from the same published evaluation records. Refresh existing coverage or clearly label the archive with its source/as-of date. Retain model/configuration/dataset on result → task navigation. Link each summary to its underlying public attempts where available; show explicit unavailability otherwise.
acceptance_checks: Both example tasks expose source and as-of metadata.
0934a4d8 can distinguish the archived table from newer official Opus4.6 data.
Following a current model result into a task retains context or clearly says it is unavailable.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Make legacy task table sorting and explanations keyboard accessible
tickets.observation: Source creates sortable th elements with pointer click sorting; no tabindex/button/key handlers/aria-sort found. Header tooltip code only handles mouseenter/mouseleave. Live DOM inspection confirms plain nonfocusable headers.
reproduction: Open task 0934a4d8 and use Tab to reach Model Performance.
Attempt to sort Total Cost using only keyboard input.
Compare with a pointer click, which sorts successfully.
tickets.proposed_fix: Use focusable sorting buttons in table headers, aria-sort on current column, and focus/touch-accessible descriptions.
acceptance_checks: Tab reaches every sort control; Enter/Space changes order.
Assistive technology receives column name and current sort direction.
Column definitions are reachable without hover.
tickets.qualification: Public source locator: table-generator.js:142-188,284-312; locate sort click listener in same public file
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Clarify and reconnect the ARC1/2 raw-attempt publication channel
tickets.observation: ARC Prize public HF v1 and v2 evaluation repositories lastModified values remain 2026-06-04T16:43:53.000Z and 2026-06-04T16:45:03.000Z respectively. Neither current file list contains GPT-6. The September Astra page publishes ARC1/2 results but offers task summary links rather than raw ARC1/2 attempt downloads. No replacement raw source was found in inspected public channels.
reproduction: Open https://huggingface.co/arcprize and inspect the v1/v2 public evaluation dataset histories or API metadata.
Open the Astra results page and its linked Astra blog post.
Look for the matching ARC1/2 answer grids, model responses and run metadata for a reported task.
tickets.proposed_fix: Restore publication of public-evaluation ARC1/2 raw attempts on Hugging Face, or document and link a successor store. Include submitted grids, released responses/reasoning where available, task/dataset/model/run/attempt identities and source revisions so downstream tools can ingest them. If publication cannot resume, give explicit coverage/cutoff and availability notices; a notice clarifies the gap but does not restore ingestion. Preserve historical links.
acceptance_checks: For a post-June model, a reader can either download the documented public ARC1/2 run artifacts or see a clear explicit unavailability/cutoff notice. HF cards identify any successor source.

For a newly published public-evaluation model, an independent tool can download and parse at least one successful and one failed attempt with stable identities and documented coverage. Any withheld fields are explicitly marked, not fabricated.
tickets.qualification: This is an observed four-month repository update gap, not proof of a permanent shutdown. An unlinked or private store may exist; publication policy needs the maintainers decision. ARC3 replay links are already present and must not be included in the missing-raw-data claim.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.
tickets.impact: ARC Explainer cannot ingest the newer attempts or extend its existing reasoning/grid inspection and statistics to those newer models without the underlying records. Mark identifies this as the main request, separate from the immediate website bug priorities.

tickets.title: Connect the new Results index to older evaluations and their data
tickets.observation: The Results index has 24 dated release rows, 30 linked model/submodel pages, from June9 to September29,2026; no older archive control was found. Older 2024/2025 reports remain in Blog. In official evaluation data, all 221 ARC1/2 semi-private records across 113 pre-2026 model/config IDs have blank resultsUrl; 208 of those records across 107 IDs have display:true. Current leaderboard rows link only through resultsUrl, and the renderer does not use model dataUrl.
reproduction: Open Results and attempt to find the September2024 o1, December2024 o3, or January2025 R1 release.
Open Verified Leaderboard and locate an older model such as o3-mini or Sonnet4.5.
Compare available row navigation with the surviving historical blog and HF artifacts.
tickets.proposed_fix: Add a visible historical-results/archive route and link older leaderboard records to appropriate historical reports and existing raw data. Label legacy results honestly rather than inventing current-style detail pages.
acceptance_checks: Starting from Results or Verified Leaderboard, readers can locate the cited 2024/2025 reports and their available artifacts without searching Git history or knowing the exact blog URL. Every linked archive target is checked for content, not just HTTP 200.
tickets.qualification: Do not claim the old reports or aggregate results disappeared. The raw record counts are source-data counts, not a browser row-count assertion. This is a navigation/coverage enhancement unless broader historical coverage was intended.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Expose available ARC1/2 attempts from the task performance view
tickets.observation: The intended task performance table renders Provider, Model ID, Dataset, Passed and Total Cost. It has no attempt-output or original-response link. Existing HF attempt files contain answer grids and response/run metadata; a checked GPT4o task file returned 200.
reproduction: Inspect a task Model Performance table.
Try opening the original attempt behind a Pass/Fail row.
Compare with the existing public HF attempt-file structure.
Open the exact ARC Explainer comparison links: #73914 is Opus 4.6 with populated reasoning and 2/2 correct; #56958 is Opus 4.5 with populated reasoning and 0/2 correct, recorded in November 2025.
tickets.proposed_fix: Start with source-artifact links. Then add a read-only saved-attempt drawer: submitted and expected grids per test, mismatch highlighting, available final response, recorded cost/time/tokens, and stable run/attempt links. Preserve dataset, model configuration and source revision. Keep unknown values distinct from zero; do not imply unavailable reasoning was recorded.
acceptance_checks: For one published successful attempt and one failure, the task page opens the correct output grid/response artifact with model, task, dataset and run provenance. Missing artifacts are explicitly labeled rather than linked to404s.
A wrong-size or malformed answer remains inspectable; the viewer does not crash or hide the failure.
Two attempts, multiple test pairs and task-level scoring remain distinct. Missing artifacts display an explicit unavailable state.
A shared link restores the exact task, dataset, model configuration and attempt; keyboard and phone users can inspect it.
tickets.qualification: This is an enhancement, not evidence that the official site lacks per-task comparisons broadly. Token counts/timing may vary by artifact and should not be fabricated. The sampled GPT4o file records a2026 run, not the original2024 run.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Make learning and community resources easier to choose
tickets.observation: The catalogue has 246 entries. It already links ARC-AGI Puzzle Explorer to ARC Explainer /analytics, and includes ARC Game, Brain Grid Game and MichaelPascale/human-arc. No child/family audience filter or direct entry for Mark’s Human ARC, Space Force Mission Control or ARC-3 game guides was found.
reproduction: Start at Resources as a parent, teacher or beginner looking for something immediately playable.
Try to distinguish a game, task examiner, tutorial, research paper and dated result archive.
tickets.proposed_fix: Add resource type, audience, ARC version, access requirements and last-reviewed date. Consider a small “Start here / Play / Examine model answers” collection. Evaluate Mark’s individual tools alongside existing choices using the same criteria; acceptance is an editorial choice. Review The ARC Daily news page and the curated synthetic ARC-3 game catalog as distinct entries, alongside the saved-attempt viewer and existing play/guide resources. Label synthetic games as community/research resources, not official hidden evaluation games.
acceptance_checks: A visitor can find a reviewed beginner/family-friendly activity and understand login, cost, device and reading requirements before opening it.
Analytical tools are discoverable separately from papers and videos.
Chosen entries use direct working URLs and an accurate scope description.
tickets.qualification: The site does have human-play and child-oriented resources. Mark’s Human ARC and MichaelPascale/human-arc are different projects. No child usability study or full playthrough of all linked games was conducted; do not claim a proven age rating or that one game is objectively superior.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Date the legacy guide and clarify benchmark-specific claims
tickets.observation: The guide presents ARC-AGI-1 & 2 together while some task counts and approach descriptions belong to a particular benchmark or earlier era. The public partners page also introduces its ecosystem as ARC Prize 2025 participants alongside current calls to action.
reproduction: Review Guide 1 dataset counts, approach descriptions and any claims using current/top language.
Review the partners introduction against the intended page year.
tickets.proposed_fix: Label dataset counts by benchmark/split and date historical performance claims. Link readers to current leaderboards. Explicitly label an archived 2025 partner list or update its introduction if intended to be current.
acceptance_checks: A newcomer can tell which benchmark and date every count/performance claim refers to.
Historical claims remain accurate as history rather than being silently rewritten as current results.
tickets.qualification: Editorial review, not an allegation that every old tutorial or partner entry is wrong. Matt should choose whether to update or preserve an explicitly dated archive.
tickets.decision: For Matt to triage; not yet approved or implemented.

tickets.title: Reconcile the summit application call to action with its deadline
tickets.observation: On October 8 the page still promotes Apply to present, while its linked form specifies a September 14, 2026 deadline. The summit is October 23. The form still renders questions; no submission was attempted.
reproduction: Open the summit page and follow Apply to present.
Compare the advertised application with the deadline in the form.
tickets.proposed_fix: If presentation applications are closed, label the closed state and retain the attendance route. If extended, update the deadline consistently on both surfaces.
